Moore did notch 14 targets over his first five games, but since returning in Week 10 from a stint on IR, he's played just one offensive snap over two contests.

It was another rough performance for Green Bay's ground game, which gained just 55 yards on 14 carries. Williams got two totes, and the wide receiver ended up atop the team's rushing leaderboard with 18 yards, ahead of RBs Kaleb Johnson (13 yards on eight carries) and MarShawn Lloyd (10 yards on one carry). Williams has consistently seen minor work out of the backfield this season, logging at least one carry (but no more than three) in all but one of his six appearances. That gives a small boost to his fantasy outlook, but he's yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, so Williams is a very risky fantasy play. However, he'd probably get a boost in that regard if Christian Watson (concussion), who exited late in the first half Wednesday and didn't return, isn't able to suit up in Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Brooks and Kaleb Johnson split the workload pretty evenly at running back for Green Bay, with the former logging 19 offensive snaps and the latter 24. Meanwhile, MarShawn Lloyd tallied just three snaps on offense. Whereas Johnson led the group with eight carries, Brooks was by far the most active in the passing game, tying for the overall team lead with both his five targets and four receptions. He had just four catches over five games coming into Wednesday, so it remains to be seen if the bump in work as a pass catcher continues for Brooks moving forward. The entire breakdown of the Packers backfield could shift in Week 13 against the Saints if Josh Jacobs (finger) is ready to return to action.

Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), Foster Moreau and Marlin Klein would all be in line for larger roles on offense in the event that Schultz is not cleared to play in Week 12.

Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. Given Harrison's modest production over three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, he profiles as a speculative fantasy lineup option in Week 12, with Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip, 'DNP' Thursday) also in Houston's WR mix.

Boutte has missed the first two practices of Week 12 prep while managing a hip injury that he sustained during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts in Week 11. If he doesn't practice Friday, then Boutte should be considered on the doubtful side of playing Sunday against the Ravens. Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Nikko Remigio would all be in line for larger roles in the Texans' offense in the event that Boutte doesn't play against Baltimore.

away.injury_description: If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday would factor into Tuten's potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so Tuten appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

Washington's shoulder injury seems to have taken a sudden turn for the worse, but the Jaguars had been preparing for their top receiver to be available, so they hadn't been utilizing Hunter much on offense in practice. Hunter should hold down his usual outside cornerback role on defense, but it's likely that most of the targets vacated by Washington will go to some combination of Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and CJ Williams rather than Hunter among Jacksonville's wide receivers.

Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

Striggow will be good to go for Sunday's matchup against the Titans after clearing the league's concussion protocol. The 24-year-old has compiled 13 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games this season while playing on both defense and special teams.

Mekari now has a 21-day window for the Jaguars to return him to the active roster. The right guard returned to practice as a limited participant. If Mekari can upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session, there is a chance he could be activated for Sunday's game against the Titans. The Jaguars could just as easily take it slow with the veteran offensive lineman to ensure he is healthy and ready for his return to the field, so Ezra Cleveland may be in line for another start at right guard.

Love must miss at least one more game due to the right high-ankle sprain that he picked up in a Week 8 win at Dallas, but the Cardinals have a decision to make next week, as they have a Week 13 matchup with the Eagles on tap before a Week 14 bye. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye.

Phillips was listed as limited for the second consecutive day despite managing to play through the ankle injury during the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Jack Heflin would be in line for increased playing time during Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins if Phillips ends up being unable to play.

Williams -- who was inactive in Week 11-- was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, but his full participation a day later paves the way for him to return to action Sunday against the Dolphins. With fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) in danger of missing his second straight game, Williams could end up working as the Jets' WR3 this weekend behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the event that he's active and Cooper isn't.

Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.

Wallace missed the Jets' last three games due to a groin injury, but his absence from Wednesday's report indicates that he is fully healthy and will return for Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday. Wallace has mostly played on special teams in 2026 and has four assisted tackles and a fumble recovery across six regular-season games.

Friday's final injury report will determine whether Bowers carries an injury designation for the contest or is fully cleared for Week 12 action.

Butler enterted the NFL's concussion protocol after being ruled out for the remainder of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The defensive tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact practice.

Pegues exited the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos late in the fourth quarter and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's full participation and injury clearance in the first prep session of Week 12 imply Pegues did not return to the Week 11 loss because he exited late, when the game was out of reach.

Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

away.injury_description: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Tyler Onyedim should be in line for increased playing time.

Schrader reached the maximum three games of elevation from the practice squad, but now that he's on the active roster, the Missouri product is eligible to suit up for the Broncos moving forward. He's expected to contribute as a kickoff returner, and Schrader could also settle in as the No. 2 or 3 running back behind starter Jonah Coleman in Friday's game against the Steelers with J.K. Dobbins serving a one-game suspension.

Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

Since being designated for return from injured reserve Tuesday, Badie has been listed as a 'full' participant on each of his team's three practice reports ahead of Week 12. With RJ Harvey (knee) not yet ready to return from IR and J.K. Dobbins set to serve a team-imposed suspension this week, Badie is in a position to serve in a backup role behind ascending rookie Jonah Coleman, provided he's activated from IR by Friday afternoon. Also potentially in the mix on that front is practice-squad member Cody Schrader.

Rapp was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a quad injury that he may have picked up during the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when he logged two tackles (one solo). He will not travel with the team to Pittsburgh, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. JL Skinner, Devon Key and Jahdae Barron are all candidates to see a bump in defensive snaps in Rapp's absence.

McManus scored the first six points of the game with 43-yard and 41-yard field goals in the first quarter. He added a 40-yarder in the fourth and a 30-yarder just before the end of the game. The veteran kicker has yet to try a field goal from 50-plus yards, but he's been everything the Rams could have asked for since taking over as the team's kicker in Week 7. Through five games, McManus is a perfect 9-for-9 on FG attempts and 16-for-16 on PAT tries.

After posting a career-high 61 percent offensive snap share in Week 10 against Arizona, Daniels logged just a 22 percent share Wednesday. That was still good for third among Rams wideouts behind Konata Mumpfield (90 percent) and Xavier Smith (23 percent), but Daniels didn't get a pass thrown his way. If Davante Adams (hamstring) is able to return to action in Week 13 against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, Daniels' prospects for making an impact in the passing game will likely fall even further.

Atwell logged just six offensive snaps, behind all of fellow wideouts Konata Mumpfield (70), Xavier Smith (18) and CJ Daniels (17). The Rams also gave more offensive snaps to four different tight ends. Atwell's usage is especially notable given that both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) didn't play. Nacua is out for the season, but Adams could return as soon as Week 13 versus Kansas City. Atwell is not an advised fantasy play moving forward even if Adams has to miss more contests.

Smith was used as a ball carrier for the first time this season and gained a chunk of yards on each of his totes. Aside from that, it was another quiet game for the third-year wideout, who hasn't really been able to take advantage of a wide open WR pecking order in the wake of injuries to star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring). In fact, Smith has logged less than a 25 percent offensive snap share over the past two games with the pair of stud WRs absent, so it appears head coach Sean McVay is looking elsewhere to fill the void. As such, Smith doesn't have much fantasy value given that his primary role is in the return game.

away.injury_description: Williams recorded four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to back spasms. He was not cleared to return to Thursday's game, but there doesn't appear to be much concern over his status for Week 13 given the extra rest that Dallas will have.

Spann-Ford served as the team's starting tight end for the third consecutive game as Jake Ferguson remains sidelined with a knee injury. However, Spann-Ford had a quiet outing but will look to play a larger role next week versus the Seahawks if Ferguson is out again.

Aubrey missed a kick from 40 yards out in the fourth quarter, which ended up being the difference in the game. The 31-year-old has now converted 21 of his 26 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 38 extra-point tries across 12 games this season and will look to bounce back during next week's matchup against the Seahawks.

It was a step back for Pickens after he hauled in 18 of 28 targets for 247 yards and four TDs over the prior two games. The 25-year-old wideout is the clear No. 2 option in the Dallas passing attack behind CeeDee Lamb, but the team's woeful defense and limited depth behind the duo ensures that Pickens will see big volume from Dak Prescott more often than not. Pickens will take a 62-847-6 line on 99 targets into a Week 13 clash with the Seahawks.

He was once again Dak Prescott's top downfield option, leading the Cowboys in targets, catches and receiving yards, but KaVontae Turpin and Javonte Williams were on the other end of the QB's touchdown passes. Lamb has topped 100 yards in six of 12 games this season, including three of the last four, and he'll carry a 95-1,242-9 line on 144 targets into a tough Week 13 battle against the Seahawks.

He was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's estimated report, so his ability to practice in a limited capacity Thursday indicates that he is progressing in his recovery, and a full session Friday could be enough for him to avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's game against Atlanta.

Price has been limited in each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to knee and groin injuries that he likely sustained during the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Week 11. A full practice Friday would presumably be enough for Price to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons. He has a 6-75-1 receiving line on as many targets over his last two outings while operating in an expanded role on offense in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb), the latter of whom is unlikely to play against Atlanta.

Murray appears to be drawing closer to being active for the first time since Week 8, but he may need to practice fully Friday in order to avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Falcons. He's missed the last three games due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and he likely will slot in as Kirk Cousins' direct backup once the former is healthy enough to suit up.

Felton was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough by a hip injury, but his ability to get back to full one day later gives him the all clear for Sunday's game versus the Falcons. Assuming Jordan Addison (thumb) misses a third consecutive contest in Week 12, Felton again will be a candidate for an expanded role, which has translated to nine catches (on 17 targets) for 75 yards the last two outings.

Addison's next listing on an injury report that isn't a DNP will be his first since Nov. 13, when he suffered a thumb injury that required surgery and so far has sidelined him for two games. Head coach Kevin O'Connell relayed to Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune on Monday that Addison is "progressing well" in his recovery but is unlikely to play Sunday against the Falcons. Ultimately, Addison's status for Week 12 may be clarified once the Vikings post Friday's practice report.

away.injury_description: Vaki once again served a limited role as Jahmyr Gibbs continues to handle the bulk of the workload. The 25-year-old has totaled 181 rushing yards on 43 carries, in addition to catching 11 of his 13 targets for 84 yards across 11 games this season.

Bates' missed extra point came from 48 yards out due to a 15-yard taunting penalty. The 27-year-old has now converted 19 of his 21 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 37 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

Despite the high score, Jared Goff threw only one TD pass on the afternoon, connecting with LaPorta for an 11-yard strike in the second quarter, The tight end snapped a five-game touchdown drought in the process, but he still hasn't topped four catches or 62 yards in six contests since Detroit's bye. LaPorta will take a 43-521-4 line on 64 targets through 11 games into a Week 13 clash with the Falcons.

The fifth-year wideout finished second on the Lions in targets, catches and receiving yards to Amon-Ra St. Brown (7-146-0 on 10 targets), a position that Williams is very used to finding himself in. The veteran QB topped 300 passing yards for the fifth time this season, but Goff's only touchdown came on an 11-yard connection with Sam LaPorta in the second quarter, as Jahmyr Gibbs did most of the scoring for the Lions. Goff has thrown multiple TDs in just two of the last five games, a stretch in which he's managed a 7:5 TD:INT, but he could pop for a ceiling game in Week 13 against a struggling Falcons defense.

The talented receiver did make good use of his one reception, and Downs should be busier in a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night where weather shouldn't be a factor.

Since Josh Downs arrived via trade from Indianapolis at the deadline, Rashee Rice is leading all Chiefs wide receivers in targets with 17 over the last three contests, followed by Downs' 14, Worthy's 10, Cyrus Allen's nine, Jalen Royals' (ankle) two and Andrew Armstrong's two. Worthy's average number of targets has reduced from 5.9 per game pre-Downs to 3.3 since the addition to the position group, and the former has just a 2-38-1 line during that span. As a result, Worthy is difficult to trust as Kansas City prepares to face the Rams on the road next Thursday.

Rice's production was part of the collateral damage of a night that was unconducive for offense, as the veteran receiver tied his lowest reception and receiving yardage totals of the season for a non-injury-shortened game. Rice came in riding a solid four-game stretch where he'd generated a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets, and he'll look to return to that level of production during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday.

Smith was injured in the fourth quarter of Week 12 action, but the Chiefs never announced the reason for him hitting the sideline until Reid spoke to the media afterward. If the severity of Smith's issue is enough to require an absence or more time off, Hunter Nourzad is the likely candidate to man right guard for Kansas City.

Like Josh Allen, Mahomes didn't come close to putting up his typical caliber of production in the poor weather conditions Thursday, although the latter was at least relatively efficient compared to his opposite number. However, Mahomes failed to throw at least one touchdown pass for the first time in five games, and his yardage total was his second-lowest of the campaign. Mahomes will look to bounce back in what will be an appreciably better environment for offense during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night.

away.injury_description: With Brown set to log three straight practice 'DNPs' this week,  there's a solid chance that he'll be officially ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers later Friday. If that ends up being the case, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams would be the Patriots' available WRs on the active roster, though it's possible that Romeo Doubs (shoulder) will be activated from IR ahead of Week 12 action.

The Patriots didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but Doubs has opened Week 12 prep listed as a limited participant in back-to-back sessions. The fifth-year wide receiver was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers. Doubs' return would bolster a Patriots' wide receiver group that will likely be without A.J. Brown (hamstring) for Week 12.

Stevenson hurt his knee in Week 9 against Green Bay and initially appeared slated to miss multiple games. However, he surprisingly was able to suit up in Week 10 against Detroit in Munich, Germany, though he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share and gained only five yards on seven touches. Stevenson is now off the injury report entirely to begin Week 12 prep following New England's Week 11 bye, suggesting that the knee issue is no longer a concern. The veteran running back commented Wednesday on his ability to suit up in Week 10, attributing it to "a bunch of recovery" and sharing, "(The trainers) did a good job of just getting me available again... Leg wasn't feeling 100 percent, but I was well enough to go out there and participate with the team and try to help them out a little bit," per Sophie Weller of Patriots Wire. With no practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep, Stevenson should be set to suit up this Sunday  in Los Angeles against the Chargers, when he'll be taking handoffs from QB Tommy DeVito.

Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

Schooler did not play in Week 10 against the Lions due to hamstring injury, and he missed the Patriots' four prior games while recovering from a back issue. His absence from Wednesday's report indicates that Schooler will be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers. He has four tackles (two solo) across five regular-season games while mostly contributing on special teams.
